topic: Machine0: Persistent CPU and GPU VMs from the CLI

key_points: Launch HN (YC S26, 80 pts, 2026-08-18) by founder Barnaby (ex-Upflow CTO): 'machine0 new mybox' gives an agent a persistent cloud VM, billed by the minute, from $0.013/hr up to 60 vCPU / 240 GB RAM and GPUs (H100s, H200s), with 99.99% VM-level uptime.
Positioned for 'long horizon agent compute': coding agents running 6-8h, agent-orchestrated training/RL runs taking days, and always-on agents (OpenClaw, Hermes) running 24/7.

Four pain points addressed: resources (agents saturate RAM/CPU, GPU needs), security ('--yolo' + prompt injection = exfiltrated creds), availability (closing laptop kills mid-task agent), isolation (no clean line between user and what agent needs).

Key features: suspend/snapshot/resume, persistent block storage (10GB-16TB) with '--attach' grammar, Profiles (credentials/MCP/prompts/env injected at creation), agents self-serve via CLI or MCP, reproducible NixOS flakes or Ansible/Ubuntu.

Use cases: agent fleets (pilot scopes + sub-agents each on own VM, one customer runs hundreds of machines), model optimization & RL environments (60 vCPU RL envs up for days, suspended H100 overnight for inference-speed grinding), product infra (one customer ships thousands of machines, most alive for two minutes).
Every machine is a full KVM VM (not container/sandbox): real GPU exposed to guest with actual driver, kernel-level access, no syscall-interception. Stack: TypeScript, Postgres, Redis.

Show HN (96 pts, 2026-06-15): CLI to create, provision, and snapshot persistent NixOS (& Ubuntu) VMs. Framed as 'a modern VPS provider' — VMs stay on unless switched off (99.99% uptime), static IPs, HTTPS endpoints, 1-60 vCPU, up to 240GB RAM, optional GPUs, priced per minute.

Differentiator: first-class NixOS support. A flake declares entire OS state (packages, services, firewall, users) and pins deps via lockfile; same flake.nix + flake.lock always reproduces the exact same system — 'Terraform but for your Linux'.
Reproducibility: agents can write the Nix code and test it against disposable machine0 VMs; rollback = reverting last commit.
CLI examples: 'machine0 new my-vm --image nixos-25-11', 'machine0 provision my-vm ./flake#my-profile', 'machine0 images new my-vm my-snapshot', 'machine0 new my-clone --image my-snapshot'.
NixOS flakes repo: github.com/fdmtl/machine0-nixos. Docs at docs.machine0.io.
'Powerful & Persistent VMs from the CLI' — one command gives an SSH-ready VM with dedicated CPU/RAM/GPUs, modern agents and tooling, a static IP, and HTTPS at <vm>.mac0.io.
Sizes: 1-60 vCPU, up to 240 GB RAM, not shared, 99.99% uptime SLA. GPUs: H100, H200, MI300X, L40S, RTX 4000/6000 Ada, from $0.836/hr up to 8x H200.
Suspend & resume: pause idle machine, stop paying compute, pay only image storage while suspended. Snapshot & clone: versioned images; clone identical machines.
Disks: persistent block storage (10GB-16TB), ~$0.1667/GB/month, attach at creation (--attach disk:NAME path:/abs/path) or to running VM; survives suspend/resume and VM destruction.
Profiles: bundles of MCP servers, integrations (GitHub, Claude Code, Codex), prompts, env vars injected at VM creation — 'each agent gets exactly the capabilities you choose and nothing else'.
NixOS first-class (flakes) or Ubuntu with Ansible; all images open source. 5 regions (NY, SF, London, Amsterdam, Singapore), same price everywhere.

Extra: in-browser SSH terminal, 'machine0 skills install' (first skill /create-machine turns plain-English into git-versioned NixOS project + running VM), file sync (push/pull with --watch), MCP server so agents manage their own fleet.

Official Hermes example: 'machine0 new hermes --image nixos-25-11-hermes --size medium', install + 'hermes setup' inside VM, 'machine0 sync pull hermes:~/ ~/Backups/hermes' then 'machine0 suspend hermes'.
Per-minute billing, no commitments, same price in every region. CPU from $0.013/hr (1 vCPU/1GB/25GB small) to $3.714/hr (60 vCPU/240GB/900GB 6xl).
NVMe sizes: newer-generation CPUs with NVMe for higher disk IOPS. Premium sizes: dedicated (non-shared) vCPUs, fastest single-thread performance.

GPU from $0.836/hr (1x RTX 4000 Ada, 20GB) to $4.851/hr (H100) and $4.917/hr (H200); 8x configs to $38.808/hr (8x H100) and $39.336/hr (8x H200). GPU in us-east, uk, eu, asia (not us-west); GPU VMs may run in nearby datacenter (us-east GPU in Toronto).

Billing model gotcha: machines billed while running AND stopped (resources reserved); suspend stops machine billing. Images $0.078/GB/month. Bandwidth $0.01/GiB overage (1-10TB free). Disks ~$0.1667/GB/month billed while READY even if attached VM suspended.
Wallet: minimum top-up $5, unused credits refundable; when balance can't cover 1 hour, running machines are snapshotted and destroyed (snapshots retained).

Direct competitor named in HN thread. 'Computers for developers and agents': Durable Sandboxes (disposable VMs for AI agents, by the second), VPS (persistent Linux VMs with HTTPS and SSH), Devbox (cloud dev environment), Production.
API-first, 'ssh exe.dev to see for yourself'; buy a pool of CPU/RAM/disk and get as many VMs as you like; SSH in as root with apt and systemd; persistent, private by default, shareable with IAM.
Ships a built-in web agent 'Shelley' for coding (vibecoding testimonials).

Competitor mentioned in Launch HN for non-GPU workloads: 'instant Linux boxes via SSH for builders and AI agents', pay per minute for actual usage, no subscription, no login (SSH key fingerprint is your account).

Unique: snapshots memory and processes, pay only for actual running time per minute. Commands via SSH: create, create-from-oci, list, connect, duplicate, keepalive, wakeup (auto-start on HTTP), cron (scheduled wake/run).

Community landscape comment (yetanotherjosh): 'vm for agents with handy CLI' space is crowded — Fly.io Sprites, Modal, Blaxel, Morph, Daytona, Runloop, Ascii Box, shellbox — plus incumbent mega-clouds (DigitalOcean, AWS/GCP/Azure); Blaxel is also a YC company; needs a landscape explainer.
Skepticism (sparkling): machine0 VMs run on DigitalOcean infrastructure, so given DO's already-inflated prices it 'certainly won't be cheap'.
Comparison questions: what does this give over AWS/GCP/Hetzner/DigitalOcean (prodtorok)? over Fly.io Sprites (kwakubiney)? over Modal for GPU training (nc)?

Security concern (bobbylarson): Profiles injection at creation is the easy half; revocation mid-session is hard — if a credential rotates while a box is up for days, does the running VM keep the old value until restart? Long-horizon agents make that window the real risk.

Suspend semantics questions (zodiac): does snapshot/suspend/resume keep processes/RAM alive or require restart (CRIU?), and how fast. averylostnomad: can you pause a configured VM and resume with full disk, no billing in between — how do they keep storage economically.

stats.fact: machine0 (YC S26) CPU VMs start at $0.013/hr (1 vCPU / 1 GB / 25 GB) up to $3.714/hr (60 vCPU / 240 GB / 900 GB); premium (dedicated vCPU) and NVMe tiers available.

GPU VMs range from $0.836/hr (1x RTX 4000 Ada, 20GB VRAM) to $4.851/hr (1x H100), $4.917/hr (1x H200), and $38.808/hr (8x H100) / $39.336/hr (8x H200); MI300X available from $2.849/hr (1x) to $22.792/hr (8x).

Launch HN (2026-08-18, 80 points) positions machine0 for 'long horizon agent compute' with 99.99% VM-level uptime; every machine is a full KVM VM (not container/sandbox) with real GPU driver exposure and kernel-level access, no syscall-interception.

Show HN (2026-06-15, 96 points) highlights first-class NixOS support: a flake + lockfile deterministically reproduces an identical system ('Terraform but for your Linux'); agents can write Nix and test against disposable machine0 VMs.

Billing model: machines are billed per minute while running AND stopped (resources reserved); suspend stops machine billing and charges only image storage at $0.078/GB/month; disks ~$0.1667/GB/month billed while READY even when the attached VM is suspended.

VMs run on DigitalOcean infrastructure across 5 regions (New York, San Francisco, London, Amsterdam, Singapore) at the same price everywhere; GPU sizes not available in us-west and GPU VMs may be placed in a nearby datacenter (us-east GPU may run in Toronto).
Persistent block storage (Disks) ranges from 10 GB to 16 TB, survives suspend/resume and VM destruction, and is managed via 'machine0 disks new' / '--attach disk:NAME path:/abs/path'.

Wallet: minimum top-up $5, unused credits refundable, auto-topup on by default once a card is saved; when the balance cannot cover 1 hour of runtime, running machines are snapshotted and destroyed (snapshots retained for recreate).

Security posture: SSH-only with password auth disabled, root login disabled (access via ubuntu/nix with sudo), cloud-init randomizes root password per VM, dedicated public IP per VM, network-level isolation between VMs, ufw on by default (ports 22/80/443).

Machine0 ships an official 'Running Hermes' example: create 'hermes' VM on nixos-25-11-hermes or ubuntu-24-04-hermes image, run 'hermes setup' inside, then 'machine0 sync pull hermes:~/ ~/Backups/hermes' and 'machine0 suspend hermes'.

angles: Review angle: full hands-on review of machine0 as a 'modern VPS provider' for agents — CLI (machine0 new/ssh/suspend/snapshot), per-minute billing, KVM isolation, and NixOS reproducibility.

The long-horizon agent compute angle: why agents are moving from ephemeral to always-on (6-8h coding tasks, multi-day RL/training runs, 24/7 OpenClaw/Hermes) and how persistent CLI VMs solve resource, security, availability, and isolation pain points.

Agent-fleet orchestration angle: pilot agent scoping work + sub-agents each on their own VM, MCP server for self-service fleet management, snapshot/clone for golden-master image stamping — the 'hundreds of machines spun up and torn down from the CLI' pattern.

NixOS reproducibility deep-dive: flakes as 'Terraform for your Linux', git-versioned OS config, rollback by reverting a commit, agents writing + testing Nix against disposable VMs — the differentiator vs other VM-for-agents tools.

Landscape comparison angle: machine0 vs exe.dev (sandboxes/VPS/devbox + Shelley agent) vs shellbox.dev (SSH-based, memory snapshot, no login) vs Fly.io Sprites vs Modal vs Daytona/Runloop/Blaxel vs incumbent DigitalOcean/AWS/GCP — each carving a niche.

Cost engineering angle: full pricing breakdown with suspend-vs-stop-vs-destroy semantics (stopped VMs still bill!), wallet/top-up mechanics, when per-minute persistent VMs beat serverless (Modal) and reserved instances for agent workloads.

Security angle: Profiles with credential injection at creation, the mid-session credential-revocation gap for long-horizon agents, KVM full-VM isolation vs sandbox/container approaches for prompt-injection containment.
